description: ILLARI — Innovation, Land, Location, Analysis, Radar & Imaging — es un equipo interdisciplinario que utiliza observación de la Tierra, radar SAR, análisis geoespacial y visualización de datos para comprender los cambios del planeta. Para Dancing with the SARs, buscamos transformar datos NISAR en una herramienta interactiva e intuitiva que permita identificar, analizar y comunicar cambios de la superficie para apoyar la ciencia y la toma de decisiones.
summary: ILLARI lets anyone explore how the radar signal over Guayaquil, Ecuador, changed in twelve days. It addresses Dancing with the SARs by turning two NASA–ISRO NISAR observations into an interactive before-and-after map. Readers can compare the same place on 7 and 19 October 2026, switch between two radar polarizations, and see where the return strengthened or weakened. Across the study area, the median change was +0.23 dB in HH and +0.13 dB in HV.
details:
Open the viewer and move the slider across Box A to compare the same 500 × 500 m area on both dates. Switch from HH to HV, then inspect the adjacent change map. Orange shows a stronger radar return on 19 October, blue shows a weaker return, and pale colors indicate little change.

We compared two calibrated NISAR observations acquired along the same descending track. For each of the 1,771,545 paired pixels on the 10 m grid, we calculated the difference in backscatter in decibels. In Box A, selected to illustrate a local increase, the median change was +0.67 dB in HH and +0.64 dB in HV. Both acquisitions preceded the 26 October storm. Determining what caused the observed change would require additional observations.

The viewer runs in a web browser. The public repository includes the acquisition identifiers, processing code, and instructions for reproducing the measurements from the original satellite products.

Explore Guayaquil in the English viewer. Move the slider across Box A to compare the NISAR observations from 7 and 19 October 2026. Then switch from HH to HV and use the change map to see where the radar signal grew stronger or weaker.
